content_metadata.description: The video provides a detailed guide on common reset issues with RTS motors and how to address them effectively. Presented by Auto, the video includes step-by-step demonstrations and encourages viewers to reach out for further assistance if needed.

qAndA.answer: The first step is to disconnect the motor from power for three seconds.
qAndA.question: What is the first step in the reset procedure?

qAndA.answer: Press the up and down buttons on the remote control simultaneously. If the motor jolts or moves, the reset was successful.
qAndA.question: How do you test whether the initial reset was successful?

qAndA.answer: Allow the motor to continue moving until it reaches its end position, then proceed with the reset procedure again.
qAndA.question: What should you do if the motor starts moving immediately when you plug it back in?

qAndA.answer: The motor needs to distinctly move up and down twice for the reset to be fully registered. Holding the button ensures this double movement occurs.
qAndA.question: Why is it crucial to hold the program button for more than seven seconds when completing the reset procedure?

qAndA.answer: Viewers can leave a comment on the video or send an email to info@motorise.it.
qAndA.question: How can viewers contact Motorise.it for further assistance?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi guys, it's Otto for Motorize it and today we'll be looking at common reset problems
for an RTS motor, how to spot them, how to solve them.
Now the first one is if you try to do a full reset after you've done the first successful
reset just to make sure that it has worked so that the memory is empty.
The problem there is is that the motor only accepts one successful reset procedure.
So the best course of action is once you've done a full reset, first of all just try the
buttons up and down.
If the motor doesn't respond, at least it means that it's out of its memory and so it
should be a successful procedure.
To test that, press the up and down button at the same time.
If the motor jogs and moves up and down it means you can start the programming sequence
so it means that you can start setting the end limit switches.
Now if that's done successfully, you'll be fine.
If you have another problem where you take the motor off power for the first three seconds,
you then plug it back in and the motor starts moving, then you have another problem because
it means that the programming sequence has not been ended correctly during the reset.
Now to end that programming procedure, you just press the button and hold it until the
screen or the blind goes up and down.
So when it moves up and down, you basically close the memory and you can start with the
reset procedure.
So then again, you start with three seconds off, eight seconds on, three seconds off, etc.
So then you follow the procedure and you'll be fine.
Now what's another problem that it can occur?
Once you've done the first sequence, so three seconds off power, eight seconds on, three
seconds off, you plug it back in and you can see that the screen or the blind starts moving
and your first instinct will be to press the stop button to prevent it from going up
or down too far.
Now that's the problem because that basically terminates the reset procedure.
So what you need to do, first of all, the best thing is that once you start the reset
procedure, make sure that your blind is positioned in the middle so it's somewhere halfway.
So the screen has some place to move up or down if it happens because it doesn't always
happen sometimes the motor just jogs so it goes up and down but sometimes we'll move.
Now, so when you do the sequence again, three off, eight on, three off and up again and
you see the movement, just let the screen move until it reaches its end position.
It will stop after a few seconds so normally that should be fine.
If there's any damage or if there's any danger of damage, make sure you stop it in time,
start again.
So let it move if it's possible.
Now once you've done that, you can start pressing the program button and you'll be fine.
Now what's another common area that can occur that once you've done this, so you've done
three seconds off, eight seconds on, three seconds off, you put it back in, you let it
move until it ends with its movement, then you need to press the program button on the
back of the remote.
The screen will go up and down so it will jog shortly.
The thing is, you need to hold it for more than seven seconds for it to move a second
time and often the first movement of going up and down is mistaken for a double movement.
So you need to be holding this button long enough for it to distinctly move twice.
So it's up and down, wait a few seconds, hold it until it moves up and down again.
If you don't do that, it was another full reset procedure so you need to start over again.
Now those are the common areas that you can find.
